raw_record.original_question:
下图示意我国四大区域城市化速度的阶段差异。读图回答：

<image1>

1990—2000年丁地区的城市化速度与其他地区存在明显反差，这与哪一直接相关事件有关？
raw_record.answer: decline of the old industrial base
raw_record.final_cot:
First describe the image: The figure is a line chart of "stage differences in urbanization speed of the four major regions," with the horizontal axis showing periods such as 1982—1990, 1990—2000, 2000—2005, and 2005—2009, and the vertical axis showing annual average increase in percentage points. On the right side of the figure, curves such as Jia, Yi, Bing, Ding, and "National" are labeled. Focusing on 1990—2000, the curve of region Ding is at an obviously relatively low level, forming a contrast with the higher or rising urbanization speed performance of other regions.
Then reason: Among China's four major regions, region Ding corresponds to Northeast China. In the 1990s, Northeast China was affected by difficulties in traditional heavy industry and state-owned enterprises, the old industrial base declined, and the ability of industries to absorb employment and gather population decreased, directly leading to a low urbanization speed. Therefore, the abnormally low urbanization speed of region Ding in 1990—2000 is directly related to the "decline of the old industrial base."
